executive_summary: This collection window (December 8-14, 2026) is the twenty-fifth archived window overall. Fresh search again re-checked both carried-forward CFDA institutional questions and found no resolution to either. The CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund 2026 winner remains unconfirmed by any dated, sourced coverage from CFDA, Vogue, WWD, Business of Fashion, or Fashionista -- this is now the eighth consecutive window this signal has been carried forward open, roughly eight weeks after the October 20 gala; is_prolonged_silence('cfda-fashion-fund-winner', all_reports) continues to return True. The CFDA Fashion Awards question was also re-checked, again finding no confirmed 2026 date, nominee list, or post-event coverage distinct from the Fashion Fund; this is now the third window in which the question is tracked as a real signal_id, so is_prolonged_silence() correctly still returns False at three tracked entries against the four-window threshold -- one more open window away from crossing it formally. This window's search additionally surfaced a distinct, unrelated institutional fact worth naming precisely so it is not confused with the CFDA questions: the British Fashion Council's 'The Fashion Awards' (a separate UK-based ceremony, not affiliated with CFDA) was scheduled for November 30, 2026 at the Royal Albert Hall -- a date that falls before this window, not inside it. No dated post-ceremony winner coverage of that event was found in this window's search, so, consistent with this archive's handling of other pre-window institutional dates, it is not logged as in-window content and no winner is speculated. Generic holiday-retail spending and gifting-trend coverage (NRF, Deloitte, Salesforce-style consumer data on clothing as the top gift category, value-driven shopping behavior) was found but excluded as macro retail-economics commentary rather than style, garment, or aesthetic discourse, and because none of it was tied to specific dated, in-window collection or runway content. No new genuinely in-window style/garment signal, comparable to last window's BoF VOICES finding, was independently verified this window. On balance this window is thin, and thinner than the prior window: two unresolved carried-forward institutional questions, one precisely-scoped non-event (a real award ceremony date that is confirmed but falls outside this window with no in-window follow-up coverage located), and no verified in-window style discourse.

top_signals.name: CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund 2026 winner still unconfirmed (eighth consecutive window)
top_signals.evidence: The CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund's 2026 winner gala was held October 20, 2026. As of this window's search (covering Dec 8-14, roughly eight weeks after the gala), still no dated post-gala reporting naming a winner has surfaced from CFDA.com, Vogue, WWD, Business of Fashion, or Fashionista. The most recent dated coverage available remains the June 2026 finalist announcement (ten designers: Aisling Camps, Amir Taghi, Terrence Zhou/Bad Binch TONGTONG, Emily Dawn Long, Jamie Haller, Julia Ferentinos/Juju Vera, Zane Li/Lii, George Inaki/Milamore, Claire Sullivan, Zoe Gustavia Anna Whalen), plus the previously-noted detail that Anna Wintour did not sit on this cycle's Selection Committee.
top_signals.index_note: Carried forward from the 2026-12-07 report -- same signal_id, now an eighth consecutive open window. report_schema.is_prolonged_silence('cfda-fashion-fund-winner', all_reports) returns True against the pre-this-window history (seven entries: 2026-10-26 through 2026-12-07) and remains True with this window's entry added.
top_signals.human_editor_note: Eight consecutive windows with zero indexed coverage of a named CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund winner is well past ordinary reporting lag for a program this well-covered in prior cycles. This report does not speculate about a cause -- no winner name, delay, or cancellation is claimed or implied -- it states only that the silence continues. TODO.md's open question of whether prolonged silence eventually warrants an explicit 'awaiting resolution' status rather than repeated carry-forward remains unresolved and is not decided unilaterally here; this report continues the existing carry-forward convention rather than introducing a new status value without broader review. If dated coverage appears in a future window, reconcile and close this signal_id there with a real name and source; do not edit this or prior reports retroactively without new evidence.

top_signals.name: CFDA Fashion Awards 2026 date/nominees still unconfirmed (third tracked window)
top_signals.evidence: Fresh search again found no confirmed 2026 date, nominee list, or post-event coverage for the CFDA Fashion Awards, distinct from the CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund. The most recent confirmed ceremony remains the 2025 CFDA Fashion Awards presented by Amazon Fashion, held November 3, 2025 at the American Museum of Natural History (Ralph Lauren, American Womenswear Designer of the Year; Thom Browne, American Menswear Designer of the Year). No 2026 equivalent has surfaced in search. This window's search also confirmed, precisely to avoid conflating it with this question, that the British Fashion Council's separately-run 'The Fashion Awards' (UK, Royal Albert Hall) is a distinct organization's ceremony, scheduled November 30, 2026 -- a real, dated, but pre-window event with no in-window follow-up coverage found, and not a substitute for the still-unconfirmed CFDA Fashion Awards.
top_signals.index_note: This signal_id was first added in the 2026-11-30 report; this is its third tracked entry. is_prolonged_silence('cfda-fashion-awards-2026', all_reports) correctly still returns False (3 entries, below the 4-window threshold) -- one more consecutive open window would cross it.
top_signals.human_editor_note: This entry continues formal tracking rather than backdating it. The most defensible reading remains that this ceremony's 2026 scheduling has simply not been publicized yet, or search recency/indexing has not caught up -- no cancellation or change to the awards program is implied. This report also deliberately does not treat the British Fashion Council's unrelated 'The Fashion Awards' (a different institution, different country, different history) as evidence bearing on the CFDA question one way or the other; naming it here is only to prevent a future reader or agent from conflating the two similarly-named ceremonies.
